track.legalName: Expunction after trial court acquittal, Tex. Code Crim. Proc. arts. 55A.002 and 55A.201
track.publicName: Clear a record after being found not guilty
track.mechanism: A person tried and acquitted by the trial court is entitled to expunction. Under art. 55A.201 the order shall be entered not later than the 30th day after the date of acquittal, on request of the acquitted person after notice to the state, or on request of the attorney representing the state with the person's consent. On acquittal the trial court shall advise the person of the right to expunction. The requesting party must provide the information required in an art. 55A.253 petition. The order is prepared by the acquitted person's attorney if the person was represented, otherwise by the attorney representing the state. Where the 30-day window has closed or the court did not act, the person falls back to an ordinary ex parte petition under art. 55A.251, which lists art. 55A.002 among the qualifying entitlements. Article 55A.151 bars relief where the acquitted offence arose out of a criminal episode as defined by Penal Code 3.01 and the person was convicted of, or remains subject to prosecution for, at least one other offence in that episode. Under art. 102.0061(c), read at source on 2026-08-06, the filing fee must be waived where the expunction relates to an acquittal other than one described by art. 55A.151 and the petition is filed not later than the 30th day after the acquittal.
exclusions: An acquittal arising out of a criminal episode as defined by Penal Code 3.01 where the person was convicted of, or remains subject to prosecution for, at least one other offence in that episode. Article 55A.151 bars relief outright.
An acquittal by the Court of Criminal Appeals or a court of appeals, which is the discretionary art. 55A.101 route and is modelled separately.
A mixed-verdict multi-count case, which requires T.S.N. analysis and is not auto-generated.

units.label: Request to the trial court within 30 days of acquittal, art. 55A.201
units.description: Applies where the acquittal is recent enough that the 30-day window is open. LegalEase generates a written request to the trial court under art. 55A.201, with notice to the state, together with the complete art. 55A.253 information package that art. 55A.201(c) requires the requesting party to provide, and the agency and entity list. units.label: Ordinary ex parte petition where the window closed or the court did not act, art. 55A.251
units.description: Applies where the 30-day window has closed or the trial court did not enter the order. track.venue: In-window: the trial court if it is a district, justice or municipal court of record, or a district court in the county where the trial court sits (art. 55A.201(a)). destination.name: The trial court within the window, otherwise a district court for the county of arrest or of the alleged offence
destination.detail: No statewide expunction form exists at any level of Texas state government, so there is no statewide form to be rejected locally. What varies by county is formatting practice: civil cover sheets, sensitive-data handling, hearing-setting procedure, copy counts, and whether the clerk or the filer prepares the notice of hearing. Article 55A.253(c) requires each district clerk to publish the agency and e-mail list on the clerk's website, so that list is itself county-specific and is the first place the packet sends the participant.

participantActionRequired.description: Obtain Texas DPS criminal history record. Follow DPS form CR-63, the Procedure for Review of Personal Criminal History Record Information. It is an instruction sheet rather than a form to complete: it sets out fingerprinting through the DPS FAST vendor at a $10 fingerprinting fee plus a $15 record fee, or a hard-card mail route. The DPS history supplies the TRN the order must carry under art. 55A.301, the arrest date, the arresting agency and the agency list, and it is also how the participant sees whether relief already happened. packetInstructions: Article 55A.253(a) prescribes the required contents of the petition: the petitioner's full name, sex, race, date of birth, driver's licence number, social security number and address at the time of arrest; the offence charged; the date the offence was alleged to have been committed; the date of arrest; the county and any municipality of arrest; the arresting agency; the case number and court of offence; and, with applicable physical and e-mail addresses, a list of every state and local official, agency and entity, every central federal depository reasonably believed to hold subject records, and every private entity that compiles and disseminates criminal history record information for compensation. Each item must appear or be accompanied by an explanation of why it is not included. That specificity is what makes a controlled pleading supportable in a state with no form.
scopeRestrictions: TexasLawHelp forms carry non-commercial site terms and may not be filled and delivered inside a paid product. Confirmed on 2026-08-06 that texaslawhelp.org is operated by the Texas Legal Services Center as a legal-aid self-help site and that its expunction forms are neither promulgated nor mandatory nor statewide court forms. The Texas Justice Court Training Center forms are training aids for justice and municipal courts published by Texas State University, likewise not statewide court forms. County and district clerk packets are local only. LegalEase drafts its own petition and order to arts. 55A.253 and 55A.301 and uses none of these as a form.

track.mechanism: A person convicted of a misdemeanour and placed on community supervision under a Chapter 42A provision other than Subchapter C — straight probation rather than deferred adjudication, including split sentences — who successfully completed it. The waiting period is immediate on completion of community supervision, except that a misdemeanour under Penal Code Chapters 20, 21, 22, 25, 42, 43 or 46 waits until the second anniversary of completion. Completion means the full supervision period including any term of confinement and payment of all fines, costs and restitution. This is the ordinary route for a probated misdemeanour conviction and is probably the highest-volume conviction track in the state. Section 411.073 was last amended in 2017 and was not touched in 2025 or 2026.
exclusions: Straight time served, or deferred adjudication. Those route to Gov't Code 411.0735 and 411.0725 respectively.
Community supervision that was revoked.
Failure to complete the supervision period, including any term of confinement and payment of all fines, costs and restitution.
Conviction of or deferred adjudication for another offence, other than a fine-only traffic offence, between placement on community supervision and expiration of any applicable waiting period.
Alcoholic Beverage Code 106.041, and Penal Code 49.04, 49.05, 49.06 and 49.065, and any offence under Penal Code Chapter 71.

Ever previously convicted of or placed on deferred adjudication for an offence requiring sex offender registration; aggravated kidnapping under Penal Code 20.04; murder under 19.02; capital murder under 19.03; trafficking of persons under 20A.02; continuous trafficking under 20A.03; injury to a child, elderly individual or disabled individual under 22.04; abandoning or endangering a child under 22.041; violation of certain court orders under 25.07; repeated violation of certain court orders under 25.072; stalking under 42.072; or any other offence involving family violence as defined by Family Code 71.004. This includes the offence for which the order is sought.
A court affirmative finding that the offence involved family violence.
Conviction of or deferred adjudication for another offence, excluding fine-only traffic offences, during the supervision or sentence period and during any applicable waiting period.

track.mechanism: Deferred adjudication community supervision resulting in discharge and dismissal, where the person does not qualify under Gov't Code 411.072. The court shall issue the order after notice to the state, an opportunity for a hearing, and a determination of entitlement and best interest of justice. track.legalName: Order of nondisclosure after community supervision following a DWI conviction, Tex. Gov't Code 411.0731
track.publicName: Seal a DWI conviction after successfully completing probation
track.mechanism: A conviction for DWI punishable as a Class B misdemeanour under Penal Code 49.04, other than an offence punishable under 49.04(d), followed by community supervision under a Chapter 42A provision other than Subchapter C which the person completed. The waiting period is the second anniversary of completing community supervision where the person successfully complied with a condition requiring an ignition interlock device for six months or longer, and otherwise the fifth anniversary. Section 411.0731(c) expressly requires the petition to include evidence that the person is entitled to file it. Under 411.0731(e) a court may not issue the order if the attorney representing the state presents evidence sufficient to the court demonstrating that the offence resulted in a motor vehicle collision involving another person, including a passenger. The person remains eligible if the court waived all or part of the fine and costs. The section was last amended in 2023 and was not touched in 2025 or 2026.
exclusions: DWI as a Class A misdemeanour or higher, an offence punishable under Penal Code 49.04(d), or an alcohol concentration of 0.15 or more.
Deferred adjudication rather than post-conviction community supervision, which routes to Gov't Code 411.0726.

Community supervision that was revoked, or not completed including confinement and payment of all fines, costs and restitution. Waiver of all or part of the fine and costs by the court does not disqualify.
Any prior conviction or deferred adjudication other than a fine-only traffic offence. This section is for first-time offenders only.
An offence that resulted in a motor vehicle accident involving another person, including a passenger, even without injury.

This includes the offence for which the order is sought.
A court affirmative finding that the offence involved family violence.

track.mechanism: Successful completion of a veterans treatment court programme as defined by Government Code Chapter 124 or former law. The waiting period is the second anniversary of the date of successful completion, and a felony conviction at any time during those two years defeats it. The OCA nondisclosure documents are statewide MODEL forms, not mandatory and not promulgated. Confirmed on 2026-08-06 from the Texas Judicial Branch nondisclosure forms page and from the document footers themselves, which read OCA MODEL PETITION and are dated February 2022, with the Overview dated February 2024. Gov't Code 411.0745(c) and (d) do direct OCA to prescribe and publish a form for petitions filed electronically or by mail, and every county and district clerk website must link to it, so these sit closer to a statutorily authorised statewide model than to a sample. Nothing in Subchapter E-1 makes the OCA form mandatory or forbids a differently drafted petition, and the packet does not assert that it is mandatory.
An order of nondisclosure applies to one offence. Multiple offences require multiple orders, and that is a cost and packet multiplier the participant must be told about before paying.

Nondisclosure seals rather than destroys.
